Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National FDA targets WHO Listed Authority status as it marks 30th anniversary Source : Michelle Lartey 25 November 2026 3:09am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) is working towards attaining World Health Organisation (WHO) Listed Authority status as part of efforts to strengthen Ghana’s position in global health regulation.
Chief Executive Officer of the FDA, Professor Kwabena Frimpong-Manso Opuni, announced the ambition at the launch of the Authority’s 30th anniversary celebrations in Accra on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.
He said the Authority was taking steps to secure the recognition, which would further strengthen its standing among regulatory institutions meeting internationally recognised standards.
“Our ambition is not simply to be an effective national regulator, but to be a trusted regulatory partner and a centre of excellence that contributes meaningfully to public health protection across Africa,” he said.
The ambition builds on progress made by the FDA in strengthening its regulatory systems over the past three decades.
The Authority attained WHO Maturity Level Three status in 2020, which was successfully re-benchmarked in January 2025. Its clinical trials and pharmacovigilance functions have also attained WHO Maturity Level Four.
The FDA’s laboratory is accredited for 63 tests, while the Authority has been designated a Regional Centre of Excellence by the African Medicines Regulatory Harmonisation initiative, enabling it to support the training of regulators across the continent.
Professor Opuni said the next phase of the Authority’s development would require it to respond to an increasingly complex regulatory environment.
He cited advances in medicines and therapies, artificial intelligence, digital health solutions and increasingly complex global supply chains as developments requiring stronger regulatory systems.
“We must therefore ensure that the FDA does not simply preserve its achievements, but builds on them to become a more responsive, innovative, efficient, and globally respected regulatory institution,” he said.
A new strategic plan covering 2026 to 2030 is expected to guide the transition, with priorities including digital regulation, modern infrastructure, staff development and stronger partnerships.
The FDA also plans to strengthen its support for local pharmaceutical manufacturing as government pursues a target of producing 70 per cent of the country’s pharmaceutical needs locally.
Professor Opuni said the Authority would provide the regulatory framework needed to support the growth of domestic pharmaceutical production.
As it marks 30 years of operations, the FDA says maintaining public confidence will require cooperation among manufacturers, distributors, importers, health professionals and consumers.
